messages:
rachel: Heads up: starter app users keep hitting import errors on edge platforms. Example from Vercel Edge: 
```error
Error: Cannot find module '@redwood/infer-sdk'
```

omar: Are they using `import` or `require`? Vercel Edge prefers ESM. If the package resolves to CJS by default, bundlers can fail.

eli: I dug in. Our package.json currently has: 
```json
{"main":"dist/cjs/index.js","module":"dist/esm/index.js","types":"dist/index.d.ts"}
```
No conditional `exports`. Old school fields confuse modern runtimes.

tara: Yep. We should add an `exports` map so Node, bundlers, and edge runtimes pick correct entrypoints. Something like:
```json
{"exports": {".": {"require": "./dist/cjs/index.js","import": "./dist/esm/index.js","default": "./dist/esm/index.js"}}}
```
But how do we signal an edge-specific build? Some libs use a non-standard `edge` condition.

rachel: Another angle: Deno and Bun behave differently. Bun respects `module` and `exports` but also has its own resolver quirks. We should add smoke tests in CI for Bun and Deno.

omar: Also typings: when `exports` is present, TS sometimes can't find the types unless `types` points to a file at the package root or subpath exports include `types`. Consider adding `{"types": "./dist/index.d.ts", "exports": {"./package.json": "./package.json"}}` to avoid breakage.

eli: For edge builds: produce an explicit `dist/edge/index.mjs` that avoids node-only code. Replace `crypto` usage with `globalThis.crypto` and avoid `process.env` at top-level. Lazy-evaluate env at runtime via constructor options so bundlers won't include node shims.

tara: Retries are a separate headache. Our backoff uses `setTimeout` + `setImmediate` shim. On Workers `setImmediate` doesn't exist and polyfills break. We should move to a scheduler abstraction: call-site supplies timers or we use `setTimeout` and Promise delays only.

rachel: Good point. Also AbortController differences: some edge platforms implement it but signals behave slightly different when used with fetch; we saw tests where abort didn't cancel the retry loop.

omar: We can accept an AbortSignal passed into the request method and make retry logic observe it. That avoids depending on global polyfills.

eli: On publishing strategy: two options again: single package with exports (cjs+esm+edge) vs separate `-edge` package. I'm leaning single package but with clear docs and a tiny edge artifact to keep installs simple.

tara: If single package, make the edge subpath explicit: `exports: {".": {"import":"./dist/esm/index.js","require":"./dist/cjs/index.js"},"./edge": {"import":"./dist/edge/index.mjs"}}` then users can `import sdk from '@redwood/infer-sdk/edge'` when they need it.

rachel: We should also add a small `wrangler` sample under `examples/worker` in the repo that uses `import sdk from '@redwood/infer-sdk/edge'` and a tiny readme for onboarding.

ci-bot: ci: edge-smoke-tests failed on cloudflare-workers (1 test). Failure: Abort logic didn't cancel retry loop. See details at https://ci.internal/1234

omar: I'll take the CI failure. Plan: patch retry to respect passed AbortSignal and add a fallback timeout for stuck promises.

eli: I'll prepare a release plan: publish v2.1.1 with `exports` + edge subpath + types at root. We'll keep `main/module` temporarily for older bundlers.

tara: One gotcha to add to the RFC: TS <4.5 + rollup versions may need `preserveSymlinks` and `conditions` adjustments. Put a note in the migration doc.

rachel: Nice. If you all agree, I'll open PRs: 1) build outputs for edge, 2) package.json changes, 3) example worker, 4) retry fix + tests. Small incremental PRs so we can iterate.

omar: +1

eli: +1

tara: +1 :rocket:
